title: Desk Guidance: Cash Pickup Sending Ceilings and Recipient Frequency Cap
content:
## The rule

A Cash Pickup transfer is booked only under the customer's own Personal Sender Account, and only while that account's status is active.

Its principal must fit every ceiling of the sending limits for the account's level at the moment of booking. Those limits are aggregated over all of the customer's personal transfers in Bank Deposit, Cash Pickup and Mobile Wallet.

The principal must also lie between the tier's smallest and largest principal, both inclusive. It may not exceed the corridor's cap, which is the most the payout network pays in one pickup.

No more Cash Pickup transfers to one recipient may be booked than the tier's figure for a rolling 24 hours, counted including the new one.

The binding ceiling for one transfer is the lowest of three figures: the per-transfer limit of the account's level, the tier's largest principal and the corridor cap.

A booking over any ceiling is not made. Paloma never splits one requested amount into several pickups.

## What the system must show

- **Account.** The account on record is the customer's own Personal Sender Account, and its status on record is active. The transfer is booked under that same account. A customer's statement about the account does not replace its recorded status.
- **Aggregate limits.** The principal is measured against the level's sending limits as they stand at the moment of booking. The customer's personal transfers in all three delivery methods count.

## How the recipient count works

The count covers Cash Pickup transfers to the same saved recipient booked strictly later than 24 hours before now. Transfers whose status is cancelled or refunded are left out. The new booking is counted in.

Hypothetical illustration with a tier figure of 3:

| Counted transfers to that recipient already in the window | Count including the new booking | Booking |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | 2 | may be made |
| 2 | 3 | may be made |
| 3 | 4 | not made |

A transfer booked exactly 24 hours before now is no longer inside the window, because the window takes only bookings strictly later than that moment. A cancelled transfer to the same recipient inside the window is not counted.

## Binding ceiling (hypothetical figures)

- An account level per-transfer limit of 4,000.00 USD, a tier largest principal of 5,000.00 and a corridor cap of 1,500.00 give a binding ceiling of 1,500.00.
- A request for 1,800.00 under those figures is over the ceiling, so the booking is not made. It is not split into a 1,500.00 pickup and a 300.00 pickup.
- A request below the tier's smallest principal is not made either, while a principal exactly equal to the smallest or the largest principal is inside the range.
